questions.question: According to Kirchhoff Current Law (KCL), the algebraic sum of currents entering a node is equal to:
options: Sum of voltages in the loop
questions.explanation: KCL is based on the law of conservation of electric charge: sum of entering currents = sum of leaving currents, i.e., algebraic sum = 0.

questions.question: Thevenin theorem replaces an active two-terminal linear network by:
options: An ideal current source in parallel with resistance
An ideal voltage source in series with resistance
An ideal voltage source in parallel with inductance
A pure resistance with no source
questions.explanation: Thevenin equivalent consists of an open-circuit voltage source (Vth) in series with equivalent resistance (Rth).

questions.question: Under the condition of Maximum Power Transfer in a DC network, the power transfer efficiency is:
questions.explanation: When load resistance equals internal source resistance (RL = Rth), half the total generated power is dissipated in Rth and half in RL, giving 50% efficiency.

questions.question: Which of the following theorems can be applied to both linear and non-linear networks?
questions.explanation: Tellegen theorem is applicable to any lumped network whether linear or non-linear, passive or active, time-invariant or time-varying.

questions.question: In a series RLC circuit at resonant frequency, the power factor of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: At resonance, inductive reactance cancels capacitive reactance (XL = XC), so impedance is purely resistive (Z = R) and power factor is unity (cos 0 = 1).
